metricRows.name: Hyporheic Exchange Indicators

inputs.label: Channel slope
inputs.rationale: Slope sets the vertical hydraulic gradient that drives bedform-driven bed exchange, the dominant hyporheic pathway in steeper channels.

inputs.label: Reach sinuosity
inputs.rationale: Sinuosity indicates lateral exchange through meander necks and point bars, the dominant hyporheic pathway in low-gradient meandering channels. Because the better pathway governs, sinuosity understated by generalized reach geometry can only fail to credit lateral exchange, never lower the rating.

limitations: Slope screens vertical bedform-driven exchange and sinuosity screens lateral meander-driven exchange. Bed hydraulic conductivity is a co-dominant control that is unavailable, so steep reaches over bedrock or fine beds can overpredict exchange.
The better pathway governs because vertical and lateral exchange are alternative mechanisms. Either alone indicates exchange potential.

Sinuosity measured over generalized reach geometry understates planform sinuosity. Under the better-pathway rule that bias can only fail to lift a rating, never lower one. The earlier weighted slope and sinuosity composite was retired for exactly that downward bias.
A result computed from one pathway is labeled partial.
The slope and sinuosity bands are screening judgments, not published thresholds.

metricRows.note: slope 0.0099 m/m (Good), sinuosity 1.234 (Good). The better pathway governs. Slope screens vertical bedform-driven exchange and sinuosity screens lateral meander-driven exchange. Bed hydraulic conductivity is unavailable, so steep bedrock or fine-bedded reaches can overpredict exchange.

metricRows.name: Hyporheic Exchange Indicators

inputs.label: Channel slope
inputs.rationale: Slope sets the vertical hydraulic gradient that drives bedform-driven bed exchange, the dominant hyporheic pathway in steeper channels.

inputs.label: Reach sinuosity

limitations: Slope screens vertical bedform-driven exchange and sinuosity screens lateral meander-driven exchange. Bed hydraulic conductivity is a co-dominant control that is unavailable, so steep reaches over bedrock or fine beds can overpredict exchange.
The better pathway governs because vertical and lateral exchange are alternative mechanisms. Either alone indicates exchange potential.

Sinuosity measured over generalized reach geometry understates planform sinuosity. Under the better-pathway rule that bias can only fail to lift a rating, never lower one. The earlier weighted slope and sinuosity composite was retired for exactly that downward bias.

The slope and sinuosity bands are screening judgments, not published thresholds.

metricRows.name: Hyporheic Exchange Indicators

inputs.label: Channel slope
inputs.rationale: Slope sets the vertical hydraulic gradient that drives bedform-driven bed exchange, the dominant hyporheic pathway in steeper channels.

inputs.label: Reach sinuosity

limitations: Slope screens vertical bedform-driven exchange and sinuosity screens lateral meander-driven exchange. Bed hydraulic conductivity is a co-dominant control that is unavailable, so steep reaches over bedrock or fine beds can overpredict exchange.
The better pathway governs because vertical and lateral exchange are alternative mechanisms. Either alone indicates exchange potential.

Sinuosity measured over generalized reach geometry understates planform sinuosity. Under the better-pathway rule that bias can only fail to lift a rating, never lower one. The earlier weighted slope and sinuosity composite was retired for exactly that downward bias.

The slope and sinuosity bands are screening judgments, not published thresholds.

metricRows.name: Hyporheic Exchange Indicators

inputs.label: Channel slope
inputs.rationale: Slope sets the vertical hydraulic gradient that drives bedform-driven bed exchange, the dominant hyporheic pathway in steeper channels.

inputs.label: Reach sinuosity
inputs.rationale: Sinuosity indicates lateral exchange through meander necks and point bars, the dominant hyporheic pathway in low-gradient meandering channels. Because the better pathway governs, sinuosity understated by generalized reach geometry can only fail to credit lateral exchange, never lower the rating.

limitations: Slope screens vertical bedform-driven exchange and sinuosity screens lateral meander-driven exchange. Bed hydraulic conductivity is a co-dominant control that is unavailable, so steep reaches over bedrock or fine beds can overpredict exchange.
The better pathway governs because vertical and lateral exchange are alternative mechanisms. Either alone indicates exchange potential.

Sinuosity measured over generalized reach geometry understates planform sinuosity. Under the better-pathway rule that bias can only fail to lift a rating, never lower one. The earlier weighted slope and sinuosity composite was retired for exactly that downward bias.
A result computed from one pathway is labeled partial.
The slope and sinuosity bands are screening judgments, not published thresholds.

metricRows.note: slope 0.0099 m/m (Good), sinuosity 1.234 (Good). The better pathway governs. Slope screens vertical bedform-driven exchange and sinuosity screens lateral meander-driven exchange. metricRows.name: Hyporheic Exchange Indicators

inputs.label: Channel slope
inputs.rationale: Slope sets the vertical hydraulic gradient that drives bedform-driven bed exchange, the dominant hyporheic pathway in steeper channels.

inputs.label: Reach sinuosity
inputs.rationale: Sinuosity indicates lateral exchange through meander necks and point bars, the dominant hyporheic pathway in low-gradient meandering channels. Because the better pathway governs, sinuosity understated by generalized reach geometry can only fail to credit lateral exchange, never lower the rating.

limitations: Slope screens vertical bedform-driven exchange and sinuosity screens lateral meander-driven exchange. Bed hydraulic conductivity is a co-dominant control that is unavailable, so steep reaches over bedrock or fine beds can overpredict exchange.
The better pathway governs because vertical and lateral exchange are alternative mechanisms. Either alone indicates exchange potential.

Sinuosity measured over generalized reach geometry understates planform sinuosity. Under the better-pathway rule that bias can only fail to lift a rating, never lower one. The earlier weighted slope and sinuosity composite was retired for exactly that downward bias.
A result computed from one pathway is labeled partial.
The slope and sinuosity bands are screening judgments, not published thresholds.

metricRows.note: slope 0.0049 m/m (Fair), sinuosity 1.009 (Poor). The better pathway governs. Slope screens vertical bedform-driven exchange and sinuosity screens lateral meander-driven exchange. limitations: Slope screens vertical bedform-driven exchange and sinuosity screens lateral meander-driven exchange. Bed hydraulic conductivity is a co-dominant control that is unavailable, so steep reaches over bedrock or fine beds can overpredict exchange.

Sinuosity measured over generalized reach geometry understates planform sinuosity. Under the better-pathway rule that bias can only fail to lift a rating, never lower one. The earlier weighted slope and sinuosity composite was retired for exactly that downward bias.

metricRows.name: Hyporheic Exchange Indicators

inputs.label: Channel slope
inputs.rationale: Slope sets the vertical hydraulic gradient that drives bedform-driven bed exchange, the dominant hyporheic pathway in steeper channels.

inputs.label: Reach sinuosity
inputs.rationale: Sinuosity indicates lateral exchange through meander necks and point bars, the dominant hyporheic pathway in low-gradient meandering channels. Because the better pathway governs, sinuosity understated by generalized reach geometry can only fail to credit lateral exchange, never lower the rating.

limitations: Slope screens vertical bedform-driven exchange and sinuosity screens lateral meander-driven exchange. Bed hydraulic conductivity is a co-dominant control that is unavailable, so steep reaches over bedrock or fine beds can overpredict exchange.
The better pathway governs because vertical and lateral exchange are alternative mechanisms. Either alone indicates exchange potential.

Sinuosity measured over generalized reach geometry understates planform sinuosity. Under the better-pathway rule that bias can only fail to lift a rating, never lower one. The earlier weighted slope and sinuosity composite was retired for exactly that downward bias.
A result computed from one pathway is labeled partial.
The slope and sinuosity bands are screening judgments, not published thresholds.

Sinuosity measured over generalized reach geometry understates planform sinuosity. Under the better-pathway rule that bias can only fail to lift a rating, never lower one. The earlier weighted slope and sinuosity composite was retired for exactly that downward bias.

inputs.rationale: Slope sets the vertical hydraulic gradient that drives bedform-driven bed exchange, the dominant hyporheic pathway in steeper channels.

Because the better pathway governs, sinuosity understated by generalized reach geometry can only fail to credit lateral exchange, never lower the rating.

limitations: Slope screens vertical bedform-driven exchange and sinuosity screens lateral meander-driven exchange. Bed hydraulic conductivity is a co-dominant control that is unavailable, so steep reaches over bedrock or fine beds can overpredict exchange.
The better pathway governs because vertical and lateral exchange are alternative mechanisms. Either alone indicates exchange potential.

Sinuosity measured over generalized reach geometry understates planform sinuosity. Under the better-pathway rule that bias can only fail to lift a rating, never lower one. The earlier weighted slope and sinuosity composite was retired for exactly that downward bias.

The slope and sinuosity bands are screening judgments, not published thresholds.

metricRows.name: Hyporheic Exchange Indicators

inputs.label: Channel slope
inputs.rationale: Slope sets the vertical hydraulic gradient that drives bedform-driven bed exchange, the dominant hyporheic pathway in steeper channels.

inputs.label: Reach sinuosity
inputs.rationale: Sinuosity indicates lateral exchange through meander necks and point bars, the dominant hyporheic pathway in low-gradient meandering channels. Because the better pathway governs, sinuosity understated by generalized reach geometry can only fail to credit lateral exchange, never lower the rating.

limitations: Slope screens vertical bedform-driven exchange and sinuosity screens lateral meander-driven exchange. Bed hydraulic conductivity is a co-dominant control that is unavailable, so steep reaches over bedrock or fine beds can overpredict exchange.
The better pathway governs because vertical and lateral exchange are alternative mechanisms. Either alone indicates exchange potential.

Sinuosity measured over generalized reach geometry understates planform sinuosity. Under the better-pathway rule that bias can only fail to lift a rating, never lower one. The earlier weighted slope and sinuosity composite was retired for exactly that downward bias.

metricRows.name: Hyporheic Exchange Indicators

inputs.label: Channel slope
inputs.rationale: Slope sets the vertical hydraulic gradient that drives bedform-driven bed exchange, the dominant hyporheic pathway in steeper channels.

inputs.label: Reach sinuosity
inputs.rationale: Sinuosity indicates lateral exchange through meander necks and point bars, the dominant hyporheic pathway in low-gradient meandering channels. Because the better pathway governs, sinuosity understated by generalized reach geometry can only fail to credit lateral exchange, never lower the rating.

limitations: Slope screens vertical bedform-driven exchange and sinuosity screens lateral meander-driven exchange. Bed hydraulic conductivity is a co-dominant control that is unavailable, so steep reaches over bedrock or fine beds can overpredict exchange.
The better pathway governs because vertical and lateral exchange are alternative mechanisms. Either alone indicates exchange potential.

Sinuosity measured over generalized reach geometry understates planform sinuosity. Under the better-pathway rule that bias can only fail to lift a rating, never lower one. The earlier weighted slope and sinuosity composite was retired for exactly that downward bias.
A result computed from one pathway is labeled partial.
The slope and sinuosity bands are screening judgments, not published thresholds.

metricRows.note: slope 0.0261 m/m (Good), sinuosity 1.056 (Fair). The better pathway governs. Slope screens vertical bedform-driven exchange and sinuosity screens lateral meander-driven exchange. Bed hydraulic conductivity is unavailable, so steep bedrock or fine-bedded reaches can overpredict exchange.

metricRows.name: Hyporheic Exchange Indicators

inputs.label: Channel slope
inputs.rationale: Slope sets the vertical hydraulic gradient that drives bedform-driven bed exchange, the dominant hyporheic pathway in steeper channels.

inputs.label: Reach sinuosity
inputs.rationale: Sinuosity indicates lateral exchange through meander necks and point bars, the dominant hyporheic pathway in low-gradient meandering channels. Because the better pathway governs, sinuosity understated by generalized reach geometry can only fail to credit lateral exchange, never lower the rating.

limitations: Slope screens vertical bedform-driven exchange and sinuosity screens lateral meander-driven exchange. Bed hydraulic conductivity is a co-dominant control that is unavailable, so steep reaches over bedrock or fine beds can overpredict exchange.
The better pathway governs because vertical and lateral exchange are alternative mechanisms. Either alone indicates exchange potential.

Sinuosity measured over generalized reach geometry understates planform sinuosity. Under the better-pathway rule that bias can only fail to lift a rating, never lower one. The earlier weighted slope and sinuosity composite was retired for exactly that downward bias.
A result computed from one pathway is labeled partial.
The slope and sinuosity bands are screening judgments, not published thresholds.

inputs.rationale: Slope sets the vertical hydraulic gradient that drives bedform-driven bed exchange, the dominant hyporheic pathway in steeper channels.

inputs.rationale: Sinuosity indicates lateral exchange through meander necks and point bars, the dominant hyporheic pathway in low-gradient meandering channels. Because the better pathway governs, sinuosity understated by generalized reach geometry can only fail to credit lateral exchange, never lower the rating.

limitations: Slope screens vertical bedform-driven exchange and sinuosity screens lateral meander-driven exchange. Bed hydraulic conductivity is a co-dominant control that is unavailable, so steep reaches over bedrock or fine beds can overpredict exchange.
The better pathway governs because vertical and lateral exchange are alternative mechanisms. Either alone indicates exchange potential.

Sinuosity measured over generalized reach geometry understates planform sinuosity. Under the better-pathway rule that bias can only fail to lift a rating, never lower one. The earlier weighted slope and sinuosity composite was retired for exactly that downward bias.
A result computed from one pathway is labeled partial.
The slope and sinuosity bands are screening judgments, not published thresholds.

metricRows.name: Hyporheic Exchange Indicators

inputs.label: Channel slope
inputs.rationale: Slope sets the vertical hydraulic gradient that drives bedform-driven bed exchange, the dominant hyporheic pathway in steeper channels.

inputs.label: Reach sinuosity
inputs.rationale: Sinuosity indicates lateral exchange through meander necks and point bars, the dominant hyporheic pathway in low-gradient meandering channels. Because the better pathway governs, sinuosity understated by generalized reach geometry can only fail to credit lateral exchange, never lower the rating.

limitations: Slope screens vertical bedform-driven exchange and sinuosity screens lateral meander-driven exchange. Bed hydraulic conductivity is a co-dominant control that is unavailable, so steep reaches over bedrock or fine beds can overpredict exchange.
The better pathway governs because vertical and lateral exchange are alternative mechanisms. Either alone indicates exchange potential.

Sinuosity measured over generalized reach geometry understates planform sinuosity. Under the better-pathway rule that bias can only fail to lift a rating, never lower one. The earlier weighted slope and sinuosity composite was retired for exactly that downward bias.
A result computed from one pathway is labeled partial.
The slope and sinuosity bands are screening judgments, not published thresholds.

metricRows.note: slope 0.0261 m/m (Good), sinuosity 1.056 (Fair). The better pathway governs. Slope screens vertical bedform-driven exchange and sinuosity screens lateral meander-driven exchange. inputs.label: Channel slope
inputs.rationale: Slope sets the vertical hydraulic gradient that drives bedform-driven bed exchange, the dominant hyporheic pathway in steeper channels.

inputs.label: Reach sinuosity
inputs.rationale: Sinuosity indicates lateral exchange through meander necks and point bars, the dominant hyporheic pathway in low-gradient meandering channels. Because the better pathway governs, sinuosity understated by generalized reach geometry can only fail to credit lateral exchange, never lower the rating.

limitations: Slope screens vertical bedform-driven exchange and sinuosity screens lateral meander-driven exchange. Bed hydraulic conductivity is a co-dominant control that is unavailable, so steep reaches over bedrock or fine beds can overpredict exchange.
The better pathway governs because vertical and lateral exchange are alternative mechanisms. Either alone indicates exchange potential.

Sinuosity measured over generalized reach geometry understates planform sinuosity. Under the better-pathway rule that bias can only fail to lift a rating, never lower one. The earlier weighted slope and sinuosity composite was retired for exactly that downward bias.
A result computed from one pathway is labeled partial.
The slope and sinuosity bands are screening judgments, not published thresholds.

inputs.label: Reach sinuosity
inputs.rationale: Sinuosity indicates lateral exchange through meander necks and point bars, the dominant hyporheic pathway in low-gradient meandering channels. limitations: Slope screens vertical bedform-driven exchange and sinuosity screens lateral meander-driven exchange. Bed hydraulic conductivity is a co-dominant control that is unavailable, so steep reaches over bedrock or fine beds can overpredict exchange.

inputs.label: Channel slope
inputs.rationale: Slope sets the vertical hydraulic gradient that drives bedform-driven bed exchange, the dominant hyporheic pathway in steeper channels.

inputs.label: Reach sinuosity
inputs.rationale: Sinuosity indicates lateral exchange through meander necks and point bars, the dominant hyporheic pathway in low-gradient meandering channels. Because the better pathway governs, sinuosity understated by generalized reach geometry can only fail to credit lateral exchange, never lower the rating.

limitations: Slope screens vertical bedform-driven exchange and sinuosity screens lateral meander-driven exchange. Bed hydraulic conductivity is a co-dominant control that is unavailable, so steep reaches over bedrock or fine beds can overpredict exchange.
The better pathway governs because vertical and lateral exchange are alternative mechanisms. Either alone indicates exchange potential.

Sinuosity measured over generalized reach geometry understates planform sinuosity. Under the better-pathway rule that bias can only fail to lift a rating, never lower one. The earlier weighted slope and sinuosity composite was retired for exactly that downward bias.
A result computed from one pathway is labeled partial.
The slope and sinuosity bands are screening judgments, not published thresholds.

inputs.label: Channel slope
inputs.rationale: Slope sets the vertical hydraulic gradient that drives bedform-driven bed exchange, the dominant hyporheic pathway in steeper channels.

inputs.label: Reach sinuosity
inputs.rationale: Sinuosity indicates lateral exchange through meander necks and point bars, the dominant hyporheic pathway in low-gradient meandering channels. Because the better pathway governs, sinuosity understated by generalized reach geometry can only fail to credit lateral exchange, never lower the rating.

limitations: Slope screens vertical bedform-driven exchange and sinuosity screens lateral meander-driven exchange. Bed hydraulic conductivity is a co-dominant control that is unavailable, so steep reaches over bedrock or fine beds can overpredict exchange.
The better pathway governs because vertical and lateral exchange are alternative mechanisms. Either alone indicates exchange potential.

Sinuosity measured over generalized reach geometry understates planform sinuosity. Under the better-pathway rule that bias can only fail to lift a rating, never lower one. The earlier weighted slope and sinuosity composite was retired for exactly that downward bias.
A result computed from one pathway is labeled partial.
The slope and sinuosity bands are screening judgments, not published thresholds.

inputs.label: Channel slope
inputs.rationale: Slope sets the vertical hydraulic gradient that drives bedform-driven bed exchange, the dominant hyporheic pathway in steeper channels.

inputs.label: Reach sinuosity
inputs.rationale: Sinuosity indicates lateral exchange through meander necks and point bars, the dominant hyporheic pathway in low-gradient meandering channels. Because the better pathway governs, sinuosity understated by generalized reach geometry can only fail to credit lateral exchange, never lower the rating.

limitations: Slope screens vertical bedform-driven exchange and sinuosity screens lateral meander-driven exchange. Bed hydraulic conductivity is a co-dominant control that is unavailable, so steep reaches over bedrock or fine beds can overpredict exchange.
The better pathway governs because vertical and lateral exchange are alternative mechanisms. Either alone indicates exchange potential.

Sinuosity measured over generalized reach geometry understates planform sinuosity. Under the better-pathway rule that bias can only fail to lift a rating, never lower one. The earlier weighted slope and sinuosity composite was retired for exactly that downward bias.
A result computed from one pathway is labeled partial.
The slope and sinuosity bands are screening judgments, not published thresholds.

floodplain-connectivity-floodplain-acces.valueText: entrenchment ratio 2.26 (flood-prone width / bankfull width, edited cross section)

scoring.equation: Rating = bands(ER); curve index is banded at 0.39 and 0.69

inputs.label: Entrenchment ratio
inputs.rationale: ER directly represents lateral floodplain width available relative to the bankfull channel.

limitations: National reference curves group channel slopes below 0.5 percent, from 0.5 to below 2 percent, and at least 2 percent.
An unsplit national reference curve is used when slope is unknown. Naturally confined valleys still require field interpretation.
Entrenchment ratio measures floodplain access; it does not establish channel stability or flood frequency.

Candidate E5b (Addendum 2, 2026-09-28, owner decision D15): the rating is withheld where the 3DEP cross-section record is unreliable on its own terms (fewer than three sections carry the ratio, bankfull is extrapolated outside the Bieger fit range, every section found its bank by the crest scan, or the reach median bank-height ratio sits at the cap only with sections the DEM cannot resolve: bankfull depth at or below 0.15 m on a 10 m or 3 m model, 0.05 m on lidar) or the ratio is physically impossible (a bank-height ratio at or below 0, an entrenchment ratio below 1). A bank-height ratio at the floodprone cap on resolved sections reads at least 2, severe incision, and is rated. Geometry is otherwise a documented gap.

rule.statement: 3DEP cross-section geometry withheld ({value}); the ratio is not rated from unreliable DEM sections (candidate E5b).
